title: What a compiler does
summary: Two computer-generated voices walk through what happens between writing code and running a program: the text is split into tokens, built into a tree, checked, tidied and translated into machine code.

claims.claim: A compiler translates the text of a program into instructions a processor can run.
claims.source: general knowledge, written for this example

claims.claim: A compiler first splits the text into small pieces called tokens, such as names, numbers and symbols.
claims.source: general knowledge, written for this example

claims.claim: It then works out how the tokens fit together and builds a tree that shows the structure of the program.
claims.source: general knowledge, written for this example

claims.claim: It checks the tree against the rules of the language and reports what does not fit.
claims.source: general knowledge, written for this example

claims.claim: It can change the program so that it does the same job with less work.
claims.source: general knowledge, written for this example

claims.claim: At the end it writes machine code for the CPU.

turns.speaker: theo
turns.say: Welcome to Briefly, How It Works. I'm Theo, a computer-generated voice.

turns.speaker: mira
turns.say: And I'm Mira, also computer-generated. Today: what a compiler actually does.

turns.speaker: theo
turns.say: Good, because I write some code, press a button, and a program appears. What happens in between?

turns.speaker: mira
turns.say: A compiler is a translator. It takes the text you wrote and turns it into instructions a processor can run. First, it splits your text into small pieces called tokens: names, numbers, symbols.

turns.speaker: theo
turns.say: Like splitting a sentence into words.

turns.speaker: mira
turns.say: Exactly. Then it works out how those pieces fit together, and builds a tree that shows the structure of the program.

turns.speaker: theo
turns.say: And if I made a mistake?

turns.speaker: mira
turns.say: This is where you hear about it. The compiler checks the tree against the rules of the language, and reports what does not fit.

turns.speaker: mira
turns.say: It can tidy the program, so it does the same job with less work. Then it writes out machine code for the CPU.

turns.speaker: theo
turns.say: So: split the text, build a tree, check it, tidy it, translate it.

turns.speaker: mira
turns.say: That's a compiler. Thanks for listening.
